Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen (Shi, Jie, Zou, Zhang); Independent Researcher (Zhu, Yang, Cao, Cai)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — Trace2Eval, a refreshable pipeline that builds coding-agent benchmarks from anonymized real user traces (trace selection, workspace and environment recovery validated by trajectory replay, human-grounded 11-dimension rubric scored by calibrated judge agents), applied to 129 tasks and 19 model-harness configurations with rubric-guided revision (R1 vs R2) and an unguided ablation

No SDD approach. Harnesses: Claude Code and OpenHands (versions not stated) within Terminal-Bench 2.0 infrastructure; non-Anthropic models in Claude Code via an Anthropic-compatible gateway. Models: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 sol, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, LongCat-2.0, Fable 5 (both harnesses), Gemini 3.6 Flash (OpenHands only). Pipeline agents: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (labelling, admission), Claude Opus 4.6 (recovery), GLM-5.3-Flash (judge), GLM-5.2 (feedback preparation)

N/A (no development approach). Per task: instance <q, W0, E0> = distilled user query, recovered initial workspace, containerized initial environment; artifact-quality rubric with 11 dimensions and human and agent score anchors (repository); revision instructions in R2

(1) Trace selection: ~20,000 sessions (June-July 2026) -> 14,603 coding traces -> 300 distribution-aligned candidates -> admission voting (5 LLM votes) + human review -> 129 tasks. (2) Context recovery: restorer, mocker, fetcher, validator agents and human review for files; environment inference, launcher, replay of recorded tool calls, tuning (typically 3 attempts), human verification. (3) Agent execution R1. (4) Artifact evaluation: task classifier, static and runtime evidence agents, judge, 3 rollouts, deterministic aggregation. (5) R2: diagnosis, design and review agents turn rubric results into revision instructions; same model revises; rescoring

None in the candidate agent loop. Pipeline: human review of borderline admission cases, human review of recovered workspaces and verification after replay, two independent human annotators plus a third adjudicator for rubric ground truth, expert setting of dimension weights

Code-quality group (35%): readability, robustness, time/space complexity, repair cost, architecture and technical choice (judge agent from source evidence)

User-experience group (interface and interaction, information presentation, feature richness); recovery fidelity (workspace acceptance, replay score); judge-human agreement (exact, within-one, usability agreement, Cohen's kappa, signed bias); judge self-consistency; total variation distance of task profiles vs traffic

Automatic with LLM judges: static-analysis and runtime agents collect source, execution and rendered evidence; GLM-5.3-Flash judge assigns grades in 3 independent rollouts, mean used for scores. Judge calibrated against adjudicated human ground truth (two annotators + third adjudicator) on 56 artifacts. Replay scores by a replay evaluation agent; workspace acceptance by human reviewers

Tasks: 129 Trace2Eval tasks in recovered contexts. Configurations: 10 models x 2 harnesses (Claude Code, OpenHands) minus Gemini + Claude Code = 19, run in Terminal-Bench 2.0 infrastructure. Held constant: tasks, recovered workspace and environment, rubric, judge (GLM-5.3-Flash, 3 rollouts), feedback preparer (GLM-5.2); R2 uses same model, harness and preserved environment. Baselines: R1 vs rubric-guided R2 vs unguided U2 (original prompt repeated). Acceptance: rubric judge, no tests. Repetitions: three samples per configuration said to be collected, variability not reported; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) 95% CIs for R2-R1 gains. Human intervention: none in runs; runs hit by rate limits or environment failures retried. Model settings 'recorded' but not stated

R1: Fable 5 best under both harnesses (92.42 Claude Code, 88.98 OpenHands); lowest R1 Total is MiniMax-M3 under Claude Code (76.64) and Kimi-K3 under OpenHands (77.54) (from Table 1; the text names no lowest model). Code quality does not determine UX (e.g. OpenHands GLM-5.2 leads DeepSeek-V4-Pro in code quality but trails by 7.48 pp in UX). Rubric-guided revision raises Total by 10.05 pp on average over 19 configurations, max +19.28 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Claude Code), min +4.95 (Fable 5, Claude Code); unguided U2 also improves every configuration but less (R2-U2 from +2.95 to +13.50 pp). Harness matters: GLM-5.3 starts at 84.76 vs 84.90 but ends 6.88 pp higher under Claude Code. Some tasks regress (Table 2). Recovery: 82.6% workspace acceptance (38/46), mean replay score 0.9175, 90.2% of 132 cases >= 0.8. Judge: usability agreement 93.0% vs 92.9% for humans; weighted kappa Agent-GT 0.173 vs Human-GT 0.542

Per the authors, yes: rubric distinguishes models by delivery quality and its feedback yields improvements beyond an unguided pass, read as evidence of rubric validity. Limitations stated: judge-human agreement leaves room for improvement (low kappa on several dimensions); recovery occasionally misses core files even after human verification; scores characterize a specific traffic population and expert-defined criteria

Judge agents reach human-comparable agreement only on some dimensions; judges being refined. File and environment recovery sometimes produces packages lacking core files, obstructing execution; further completeness checks needed. Benchmark reflects one traffic population and expert-defined criteria, not universal preferences or individual developer ability. Gap: next-generation benchmarks should be continually renewed and assess overall artifact quality in real user workflows rather than fixed-task correctness

Values from Table 1 (p. 7) and Table 16 (p. 35); Table 2 and Figures 3-5 partly garbled in the text layer. The 10.05 pp mean matches the 19 Table 1 gains. The online coding-agent service the traces come from is not named; taxonomy categories are translated from Chinese and include food takeout scenarios (Table 18). Evaluated LongCat-2.0 is a Meituan model; four co-authors are listed only as 'Independent Researcher', so any vendor link cannot be established from the text. GLM models serve as judge (GLM-5.3-Flash) and feedback preparer (GLM-5.2) while GLM-5.2/5.3 are also evaluated; the same judge's rationales feed R2 and score it. Three samples per configuration said to be collected but variability not reported. Supporting materials (rubrics, anchors, taxonomy, prompts) at anonymous.4open.science/r/TRACE2EVAL-ICLR; source traces not released (privacy, user consent). No pre-registration.
